title: In 3.5 million Gaia K dwarfs, a W1-W2 excess is not more frequent in old stars at equal metallicity; excess stars vary 4 times more often, and ZTF shows one new dust-like dimmer
abstract: Prior campaign studies found deep dust dips and a 4.6 um (WISE W2) excess on the old K-type star Gaia20cdd, but all searches selected stars by optical variability. We did an infrared-selected search. We took 4.75 million Gaia DR3 K dwarfs (G 12-16.5, |b| > 20 deg) in an old group (v_tan > 70 km/s) and a 5 percent thin-disc sample (v_tan < 40 km/s), and matched them to CatWISE2020 and AllWISE. We measured W1-W2 against the 200 nearest stars in BP-RP, Gaia [M/H], v_tan and W1. Metal-poor stars are redder in W1-W2; with a colour-only locus, old stars seemed to have about 3 times more excess. With the metallicity-matched locus, the red tail exceeds the blue tail by 2.9 +- 0.1 per 1e4 stars (old) and 0.5 +- 0.5 (thin disc) at |z| > 7, but at [M/H] -1.0 to -0.5 the values agree (3.55 +- 0.20 and 3.54 +- 1.13). The net excess increases toward faint stars, as blends do. Thus we find no evidence that the excess is more frequent around old K dwarfs at equal metallicity and brightness. 1,909 stars pass a strict rule (CatWISE z > 5, AllWISE z > 3), including Gaia20cdd; 27 percent have a Gaia neighbour within 8 arcsec (normal stars: 6 percent). Excess stars have high Gaia G scatter 4 times more often than normal stars (1.94 against 0.49 percent; blue-tail stars 0.62 percent), and 2-4 times without blends. Of 35 high-scatter excess stars with ZTF light curves, 2 are aperiodic dust-like dimmers: Gaia20cdd and the new Gaia DR3 4466400095283726080 (650 pc, v_tan 83 km/s, W1-W2 excess 0.23 mag). Of 35 matched high-scatter stars without excess, none is (Fisher p = 0.25), and of 142 random excess stars and 144 controls, none is. The new star dipped by up to 0.75 mag in ZTF r in 2021 (same-field stars changed by less than 0.006 mag), with dg/dr = 1.43 (1.35-1.51) and a chromatic 0.24 mag (g) brightening from 2018 to 2022. It is 1.5 mag above the median main sequence, so it may be a binary, subgiant or young star. Limitations: GSP-Phot metallicities, Gaia-only blend test, ZTF for a subset, no spectra.
